claim: PRELIMINARY (pilot r5-slots-003 only; 48 trajectories per half, 600 steps; the full job r5-slots-004 is pending): slots trained with the closure objective (sam_set) stay soft k-means parts, not the tracker's objects: about two slots per tracked object, high precision, low recall, mass of the matched slot unrelated to the object's mass, position recovered.
PRELIMINARY (pilot): the result is seed-stable and close to the no-learning baseline (hard segmentations of seed 0 and seed 1, and of the learned encoder and km_s6, agree).

PRELIMINARY (pilot): in its own coordinates the tracker's object view has LOWER closure ceilings than the k-means parts at every horizon (slot-set family S on 6 numbers per slot, h = 1, 2, 4, 8, 16), and captures fewer predictable nats (diagonal measure).

PRELIMINARY (pilot): the closure objective itself prefers the k-means parts to the tracker's view (objective value on the frozen readout with a head trained from scratch, 300 steps; lower is better), so the tracker's view is not a minimum the optimiser failed to find.

PRELIMINARY (pilot): fusion is where the views differ most: just after two tracked objects fuse, the best slot holds under half of the fused object (two slots stay on it), and recall recovers only after more than 16 ticks; after a fission recall is 0.8 at once.

NOT A RESULT: the pilot's sam_set_dg rows are the encoder's INITIAL weights (training was cut by the deadline at step 100 before the first checkpoint; fixed in the code of the full job). Its two seeds are identical for that reason.
